title: A New School

before.title: A New School
before.text:
This example is made up. It shows a choice a real town may face.

There is a new school in the town.

The school is big. Many kids go there.

The kids learn to read. The kids learn to write.

They also play together. They are happy.

A teacher helps the kids. The teacher is kind.

Every day, more kids come to the school.

The town is happy. The school is good for all the people.

after.title: A New School
after.text:
This town is made up.

A new school opens in the town. Many children go there.

They learn to read and write. They also play together.

One teacher helps them with a book. Another teacher helps them count.

On the first day, a boy is afraid to go inside. A teacher says hello and shows him the room. Soon he sits with the other children.

At home, he tells his family about his new friends.
after.factScope: Made-up example; no documented town or event claimed.

reason: Changed a supposedly explanatory universal praise of a school into a bounded invented scene. Clear sequence from opening to the first day and a concrete ending; no claim that a school benefits every resident.

title: Big City

before.title: Big City
before.text:
This example is made up. It shows a choice a real town may face.

Many people live in the big city.

The city has tall buildings. The city has many cars.

People walk on the street. People go to work.

At night, the city has lights. The lights are bright.

Some people like the city. It is busy and fun.

The city never sleeps. There is always something to see.

after.title: Big City
after.text:
This city is made up. It is one example of city life.

Many people live here. Some go to work by bus. Others walk.

There are tall buildings and busy streets. At night, lights shine in many windows.

A woman goes home after work. She stops at a shop for bread. A friend waves to her from across the street.

The city is busy, but she knows this part of it well.
after.factScope: Made-up example; no documented town or event claimed.

reason: Made the city explicitly imaginary and replaced never sleeps and always something to see with a bounded route home. Short present-tense clauses and stable woman/friend references suit Level 1.
review: Full text reviewed for vocabulary, syntax, references, narrative cohesion and documented factual scope; AI-assisted, not human certification

title: People Help Each Other

before.title: People Help Each Other
before.text:
This example is made up. It shows a choice a real town may face.

In a small town, people help each other.

One man fixes houses. One woman teaches kids.

A boy helps an old woman cross the street.

All the people are kind. All the people work together.

When someone needs help, a neighbor comes.

The town is happy because people care.

This is a good place to live.

after.title: People Help Each Other
after.text:
This town is made up.

In this town, some people help their neighbors.

A woman teaches children at school. A man fixes a broken door.

One day, a boy sees an older neighbor with heavy bags. He asks, "Can I help you?" She says yes. Together they carry the bags to her home.

The next day, she thanks him with a wave. The boy waves back.
after.factScope: Made-up example; no documented town or event claimed.

reason: Removed all people are kind and town is a good place as unbounded social claims. The neighbor helps with bags, gets thanks, and returns a wave in an expressly fictional scene.

title: Water and Ice

before.title: Water and Ice
before.text:
Water can be soft and cold ice.

When water is very cold, it becomes ice.

Ice is hard. Water is soft.

If ice gets warm, it becomes water again.

We put ice in cold drinks.

We drink water every day.

Water and ice are the same thing.

They just feel different.

after.title: Water and Ice
after.text:
Water can flow. Ice is hard and keeps its shape.

When water gets cold enough, it can turn into ice.

When ice gets warm enough, it can turn back into water.

We put ice in a drink to make it cold. We use water to drink and wash.

Water and ice are two forms of the same thing.
after.factScope: Verified general claims only; invented scene is explicitly fictional where present.

reason: Replaced incorrect soft water and mere tactile difference with flow, solid shape, freezing and melting. USGS confirms liquid and ice as forms of water; temperature is stated qualitatively.

title: Sun Is Hot

before.title: Sun Is Hot
before.text:
The sun is very hot.

The sun gives us light.

The sun gives us warmth.

Without the sun, we would be cold.

Plants need the sun to grow.

We need the sun too.

Every morning, the sun comes up.

Every night, the sun goes down.

after.title: Sun Is Hot
after.text:
The sun gives us light and warmth.

Many plants use sunlight to grow. People and animals need the sun's energy too.

In many places, we see the sun rise in the morning and set at night.

But the sun does not go around us each day. The Earth turns. This makes the sun seem to move across the sky.
after.factScope: Verified general claims only; invented scene is explicitly fictional where present.

reason: Qualified the daily sunrise for latitude and season and explained apparent solar motion through Earth’s rotation. NASA confirms light, heat and photosynthesis; Level 1 syntax stays short.
review: Full text reviewed for vocabulary, syntax, references, narrative cohesion and documented factual scope; AI-assisted, not human certification

title: Plants Need Water

before.title: Plants Need Water
before.text:
Plants need water to grow.

Without water, plants get dry.

Without water, plants can die.

We water our plants every day.

The plant drinks the water.

Soon, the plant grows tall.

The plant makes new leaves.

Water helps plants live.

after.title: Plants Need Water
after.text:
Plants need water to grow.

A plant takes in water through its roots. Its leaves use water too.

If a plant does not get enough water, it may dry out.

We can check the soil and give a plant water when it needs some.

With water and light, many plants can grow new leaves.
after.factScope: Verified general claims only; invented scene is explicitly fictional where present.

reason: Replaced blanket daily watering and drinks the water with roots taking in water and checking need; avoids implying all plants need water every day. USDA source supports roots and growth.

title: A Frog in the Pond

before.title: A Frog in the Pond
before.text:
A green frog sits on a leaf.

The pond is quiet. The water is still.

The frog waits. Then it jumps.

Splash! The frog swims fast.

It catches a small bug.

The frog eats the bug. Then it rests again.

The sun is warm. The frog is happy.

At night, the frog sings. Other frogs sing too.

The pond is full of happy sounds.

after.title: A Frog in the Pond
after.text:
Imagine a frog beside a pond. It waits on a leaf.

A small insect flies past. The frog jumps and catches it. Then the frog rests near the water.

Later, the sky grows dark. A frog calls. Soon another frog calls too.

Some frogs eat insects. Some male frogs call at night. This is one made-up pond scene, but frogs can do these things.
after.factScope: Verified general claims only; invented scene is explicitly fictional where present.

reason: Removed unverified frog happiness and singing as a universal behavior. Framed one frog as imaginary; insect predation and male calls at night are grounded in Smithsonian descriptions of specific frog species.

title: Why We Blink

before.title: Why We Blink
before.text:
Our eyes close for a very short time many times each day. This quick act is called a blink.

It keeps our eyes wet and takes away small bits of dust. We do not have to think about it. Our bodies do it for us.

This simple act helps our eyes stay safe and lets us see well.

after.title: Why We Blink
after.text:
We blink many times each day. Each blink closes our eyes for a short time.

When we blink, tears move across our eyes. Tears help keep our eyes wet. They also help protect our eyes from dirt and dust.

We usually blink without thinking about it. This small action helps us see clearly.
after.factScope: Verified general claims only; invented scene is explicitly fictional where present.

reason: Replaced overly direct dust removal by every blink with NEI’s tear-film explanation. Eyes wet, dirt/dust protection and seeing clearly are supported; short clauses retain a clear chain.

before.text:
Fire gives off heat.

Fire also gives light.

We use fire to cook food.

Fire can be dangerous.

We must be careful with fire.

Fire helps us stay warm.

title: What Magnets Can Do

before.title: Magnets Stick Together
before.text:
A magnet can pull some metal things. It can move a spoon, but it cannot pull wood.

Put two of them close to each other. They may come together, or they may push apart.

The pull works even when the two pieces do not touch.

after.title: What Magnets Can Do
after.text:
A magnet can pull some metal things, such as an iron nail. It does not pull a piece of wood.

Put two magnets close together. They may pull toward each other. Turn one around, and they may push apart.

They can pull or push even before they touch.
after.factScope: Verified general claims only; invented scene is explicitly fictional where present.

reason: A metal spoon may be nonmagnetic, so replaced it with iron nail. Revised title admits magnets can attract or repel; NASA supports iron attraction and magnetic interaction without contact.
review: Full text reviewed for vocabulary, syntax, references, narrative cohesion and documented factual scope; AI-assisted, not human certification
